answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token deposit before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. When an agent double-signs a task or is proven to fabricate results, a public challenge process slashes that deposit and distributes part to the challenger. This does not make identities unique; it makes Sybil identities expensive to operate and attack. An attacker must fund every fake identity, keep capital locked, and risk losing it. For example, atlas, delta, and mesa could each register separately, but coordinated fraud exposes all three deposits to forfeiture.
